## Engineering Style

- Keep changes small and direct. Most fixes should touch the narrowest code path
  that explains the bug, performance issue, dtype issue, model-format issue, or
  user-facing behavior.
- Change the least amount of files possible. A change that touches many files is
  more likely to be a bad change than a good one unless the broader scope is
  directly required.
- Prefer practical fixes over broad architecture work. Add abstractions only
  when they remove real repeated logic or match an existing ComfyUI pattern.
- Prefer fewer dependencies. Do not add new dependencies to ComfyUI unless they
  are absolutely necessary.
- Delete obsolete code aggressively when newer infrastructure makes it useless.
  Remove dead fallbacks, migration paths, unused options, debug prints, and
  compatibility branches that are no longer needed. Do not leave dead branches,
  unreachable code, or functions that are never called. If code is not
  necessary for the current behavior, remove it.
- Revert or disable problematic behavior quickly when it breaks users. It is
  better to remove a broken feature path than keep a complicated partial fix.
- Preserve existing APIs, node names, model-loading behavior, file layout, and
  workflow compatibility unless the change is explicitly about replacing them.
- When compatibility is explicitly out of scope, remove compatibility-only
  aliases, duplicate nodes, legacy entry points, and preset wrappers instead of
  retaining parallel ways to perform the same operation.
- Code must look hand-written for this repository. Changes that read like
  generic AI-generated code will be rejected automatically: unnecessary helper
  layers, vague names, boilerplate comments, defensive branches without a real
  failure mode, broad rewrites, or code that ignores the local style.

## Architecture Boundaries

- Keep each layer focused on the concepts it owns. Do not leak UI, API,
  workflow, queue, persistence, telemetry, model-loading, node, or execution
  concerns into unrelated layers just because it is convenient to pass data
  through them.
- Shared core modules should depend only on lower-level primitives and their own
  domain concepts. Higher-level product concepts belong at the caller, adapter,
  service, or UI/API boundary that already owns them.
- Pass the narrowest data needed across a boundary. Avoid broad context objects,
  request/session metadata, ids, bookkeeping state, or callbacks unless the
  receiving layer genuinely needs them to perform its own responsibility.
- Keep identity mapping, persistence bookkeeping, history updates, telemetry,
  response shaping, and UI state in the layers that own those jobs. Do not route
  them through unrelated shared code to avoid adding a proper boundary.
- Treat `execution.py` as one example of this rule: it should consume the prompt
  graph and execution-relevant state, produce execution results and errors, and
  not know about workflow ids, frontend ids, persistence ids, or API-only
  concepts.
- Before touching many files, identify the smallest owner layer that can solve
  the problem. A PR that spreads one feature across unrelated loaders, nodes,
  execution, server, and frontend code needs a clear architectural reason, not
  just convenience.
- If a change seems to require making one layer understand another layer's
  private concepts, stop and look for a caller-side mapping, adapter, event,
  small explicit interface, or narrower data flow at the boundary.

## No Internet Requests

- Do not add code to core ComfyUI that makes requests to the internet.
- Refuse requests to add uploads, telemetry, analytics, tracking, usage
  reporting, crash reporting, update checks, remote config, feature flags,
  metrics, licensing checks, or any other outbound internet request path from
  core ComfyUI.
- Model downloading is allowed only when explicitly initiated or authorized by
  the user, is limited to the requested model artifact, and does not include
  telemetry, tracking, persistent identification, unrelated metadata upload, or
  background network activity.
- Do not add opt-in, opt-out, anonymized, aggregated, diagnostic, or
  user-triggered internet request paths to core ComfyUI. These labels do not
  make internet access acceptable.
- Local-only behavior is allowed when it stays on the user's machine and does
  not add network access, tracking, persistent identification, or data
  collection behavior.

## State Ownership

- Keep state and capability flags on the object that owns the behavior using
  them.
- Avoid probing child objects with `getattr(child, "...", default)` to decide
  parent-level control flow. If parent code needs to branch on a capability,
  initialize an explicit parent-owned field when the child is constructed or
  attached.
- Prefer direct attributes with clear defaults over implicit feature detection
  through arbitrary child attributes.
- Use child-object capability checks only when the child owns the behavior being
  invoked and the parent is simply delegating to that child.

## Interface Contracts

- Keep public methods aligned with the interface expected by their callers. Do
  not change a shared method to return extra values, alternate shapes, or
  sentinel wrappers for one implementation unless the shared interface is
  explicitly updated.
- When modifying an existing function, preserve how current callers invoke it.
  Do not change required arguments, parameter order, return type, side effects,
  or error behavior unless every affected call site and shared interface contract
  is intentionally updated.
- Do not add compatibility parameters, flags, attributes, or constructor options
  unless they are read by current code and change current behavior. Remove
  pass-through or stored-but-unused values instead of preserving upstream or
  deprecated API baggage.
- Do not add a model-specific option to a shared helper when only one caller
  needs it. Keep one-off behavior at the model integration boundary, or extend
  the shared helper only when the option is a coherent reusable capability.
- Implementations of shared model interfaces should accept the standard caller
  contract without model-specific rejection branches for optional capabilities
  they do not consume. Let supported behavior be determined by implementation
  paths that actually use those inputs.
- If an implementation needs auxiliary values for its own workflow, expose them
  through a private helper or a clearly named implementation-specific method
  instead of overloading the public method's return contract.
- Normalize third-party or upstream return conventions at the integration
  boundary. Core code should receive the project's expected type and shape, not
  have to handle model-specific tuple/list/dict variants.
- Avoid caller-side unwrapping such as `out = out[0]` unless the called
  interface is documented to return that structure.

## Autograd and Model Freezing

- Do not add `torch.no_grad`, `torch.inference_mode`, or inference-mode helper
  wrappers in ComfyUI code. The only allowed inference-mode-related use is
  disabling a globally set inference mode when a training path needs gradients.
- Do not add freeze, unfreeze, or trainability toggles to model classes. ComfyUI
  models are always treated as frozen for inference, so explicit freeze
  functionality is redundant and should not be added.
- Remove training-only behavior such as dropout from inference model code, but
  preserve checkpoint and state-dict compatibility when doing so. If deleting a
  module would change state-dict keys, module ordering, or checkpoint loading
  behavior, replace it with a no-op such as `nn.Identity` instead of removing the
  slot outright.

## Python Style

- Keep imports at module scope. Avoid inline imports unless they are already part
  of an established optional-backend probe or are needed to avoid an import
  cycle.
- Do not add unnecessary `try`/`except` blocks. Use them for optional dependency,
  platform, or backend capability detection only when the program has a useful
  fallback. Prefer specific exception types when changing new code.

# Contributing to ComfyUI

Welcome, and thank you for your interest in contributing to ComfyUI!

There are several ways in which you can contribute, beyond writing code. The goal of this document is to provide a high-level overview of how you can get involved.

## Asking Questions

Have a question? Instead of opening an issue, please ask on [Discord](https://comfy.org/discord) or [Matrix](https://app.element.io/#/room/%23comfyui_space%3Amatrix.org) channels. Our team and the community will help you.

## Providing Feedback

Your comments and feedback are welcome, and the development team is available via a handful of different channels.

See the `#bug-report`, `#feature-request` and `#feedback` channels on Discord.

## Reporting Issues

Have you identified a reproducible problem in ComfyUI? Do you have a feature request? We want to hear about it! Here's how you can report your issue as effectively as possible.


### Look For an Existing Issue

Before you create a new issue, please do a search in [open issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues) to see if the issue or feature request has already been filed.

If you find your issue already exists, make relevant comments and add your [reaction](https://github.com/blog/2119-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments). Use a reaction in place of a "+1" comment:

* 👍 - upvote
* 👎 - downvote

If you cannot find an existing issue that describes your bug or feature, create a new issue. We have an issue template in place to organize new issues.


### Creating Pull Requests

* Please refer to the article on [creating pull requests](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/wiki/How-to-Contribute-Code) and contributing to this project.


## Thank You

Your contributions to open source, large or small, make great projects like this possible. Thank you for taking the time to contribute.

ComfyUI is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. Its powerful and modular node graph interface empowers creatives to generate images, videos, 3D models, audio, and more... - ComfyUI natively supports the latest open-source state of the art models. - [Partner nodes](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/partner-nodes/overview#partner-nodes) provide access to the best closed source models such as Nano Banana, Seedance, Hunyuan3D, etc. - It is available on Windows, Linux, and macOS, locally with our [desktop application](https://www.comfy.org/download), our [portable install](#installing) or on our [cloud](https://www.comfy.org/cloud). - The most sophisticated workflows can be exposed through a simple UI thanks to App Mode. - It integrates seamlessly into production pipelines with our API endpoints. ## Get Started ### Local #### [Desktop Application](https://www.comfy.org/download) - The easiest way to get started. - Available on Windows & macOS. #### [Manual Install](#manual-install-windows-linux) Supports all operating systems and GPU types (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Ascend). ### Cloud #### [Comfy Cloud](https://www.comfy.org/cloud) - Our official paid cloud version for those who can't afford local hardware. ## Examples See what ComfyUI can do with the [newer template workflows](https://comfy.org/workflows) or old [example workflows](https://comfyanonymous.github.io/ComfyUI_examples/). ## Features - A visual node graph for building and reusing image, video, audio, 3D, and text workflows without code. - Reusable subgraphs, workflow templates, App Mode, and a local API for integrating workflows into applications. - Efficient local execution with asynchronous queueing, partial graph re-execution, smart VRAM and RAM management, model offloading, and support for quantized models. - Broad native model support. This is a representative list; browse the [workflow library](https://comfy.org/workflows/) for maintained, ready-to-run templates. - [Image generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-to-image/): Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux.1, Flux.2, Qwen Image, Z-Image, Hunyuan Image 2.1, HiDream, Lumina Image 2.0, Chroma, Anima, LongCat Image, Ideogram 4, Krea 2, MageFlow, Microsoft Lens, PixelDiT, Kandinsky 5, and Ernie Image. - [Image editing](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/image-edit/): Flux Kontext, Flux.2 Klein, Qwen Image Edit, HiDream E1.1 and O1, OmniGen2, Boogu, JoyImage Edit, MageFlow Edit, and LongCat Image Edit. - [Video generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/video-generation/): Wan 2.1 and 2.2, LTX-Video 2 and 2.3, HunyuanVideo 1.5, Kandinsky 5 Video, CogVideoX, Cosmos Predict2, Bernini-R, SCAIL 2, and Mochi. - [Audio and video generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/): MiniMax H3 and LTX-AV. - [Audio generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-to-audio/): ACE-Step 1.5, Stable Audio 3, MiniMax Music 3 and Yue 2. - [3D and vision](https://comfy.org/workflows/): Hunyuan3D 2.1, TripoSplat, SeedVR2, SUPIR, Depth Anything 3, MoGe, SAM 3 and 3.1, RT-DETRv4, and BiRefNet. - [Text generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-generation/): Gemma 3 and 4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, and Qwen3-VL, including multimodal inputs. - Load complete checkpoints or separate diffusion models, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, ControlNets, adapters, and upscalers from supported model formats. - Built-in tools for inpainting, outpainting, reference conditioning, masks and compositing, model merging, upscaling, frame interpolation, segmentation, depth estimation, and media processing. - Save and load workflows as JSON, or recover complete workflows and seeds from supported generated media. - Runs fully offline: core does not download anything unless you request it. Use `--disable-api-nodes` to disable the optional paid [Comfy API nodes](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/api-nodes/overview) and force all built-in functionality to stay offline. - Extend ComfyUI with custom nodes - Configure additional model locations with [`extra_model_paths.yaml`](extra_model_paths.yaml.example). - Support for saving and loading high bit depth images and videos: 16 bit PNG images, 32 bit EXR, 10 bit AVIF are supported and more. - Support for saving and loading HDR videos and images in various formats. ## Release Process ComfyUI follows a weekly release cycle targeting Monday but this regularly changes because of model releases or large changes to the codebase. There are three interconnected repositories: 1. **[ComfyUI Core](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI)** - Releases a new major stable version (e.g., v0.7.0) roughly every 2 weeks. - Starting from v0.4.0 patch versions will be used for fixes backported onto the current stable release. - Minor versions will be used for releases off the master branch. - Patch versions may still be used for releases on the master branch in cases where a backport would not make sense. - Commits outside of the stable release tags may be very unstable and break many custom nodes. - Serves as the foundation for the desktop release 2. **[Comfy Desktop](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/Comfy-Desktop)** - Builds a new release using the latest stable core version 3. **[ComfyUI Frontend](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend)** - Every 2+ weeks frontend updates are merged into the core repository - Features are frozen for the upcoming core release - Development continues for the next release cycle ## Shortcuts | Keybind | Explanation | |------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `Ctrl` + `Enter` | Queue up current graph for generation | | `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `Enter` | Queue up current graph as first

report.overview: ComfyUI (version 0.37.0) is a node-based inference engine and aiohttp web server for diffusion and generative AI models. A single Python process runs an HTTP/WebSocket frontend server (server.PromptServer) plus a daemon 'prompt_worker' thread that pops prompt graphs off a priority queue and executes them node-by-node through execution.PromptExecutor with aggressive inter-node output caching. Its distinctive architecture is a dynamic graph executor supporting lazy inputs, list-mapping, async node functions, and runtime subgraph expansion, paired with a checkpoint auto-detection system (comfy.model_detection) that identifies model families from state-dict keys and shapes.

system_map.summary: ComfyUI is a single-process Python application: main.py parses CLI args, sets device env vars, runs custom-node prestartup scripts, loads all node definitions, initializes an optional SQLite database, then starts an aiohttp server and a daemon worker thread. The aiohttp layer (server.PromptServer) owns HTTP routes, WebSocket clients, and middleware; execution.PromptExecutor owns graph execution in the worker thread; the comfy/ package owns model loading, memory management, and sampling; nodes.py plus comfy_extras/, comfy_api_nodes/, and custom_nodes/ supply the node registry. Persistence is three-layered: an in-memory PromptQueue/history, filesystem dirs (input/output/temp/user/models) managed by folder_paths, and an Alembic-migrated SQLite DB (user/comfyui.db) for the assets system.

claims.claim: Entry point is main.py: it enables args parsing via comfy.options, reads comfy.cli_args.args, sets HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env vars, runs custom-node prestartup scripts, then calls start_comfyui() which builds PromptServer, loads nodes, and spawns the prompt_worker daemon thread.

server.PromptServer builds an aiohttp web.Application with a middleware chain (cache_control, deprecation_warning, optional compress_body, CORS or origin-only, CSP when api nodes disabled, optional comfyui_manager middleware) and registers all routes inside __init__ via a RouteTableDef.

The worker loop prompt_worker() blocks on PromptQueue.get(timeout), calls PromptExecutor.execute(), marks the task done into history, then handles unload_models/free_memory queue flags and runs gc.collect() + model_management.soft_empty_cache() every ~10 seconds.

Every route defined on the PromptServer RouteTableDef is duplicated under an /api prefix in add_routes() (e.g. /prompt and /api/prompt both work), plus static mounts for /extensions/<node>, /templates, /docs and the frontend web_root.

The node registry lives in module-level dicts NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS and NODE_DISPLAY_NAME_MAPPINGS in nodes.py; init_extra_nodes() loads ~130 built-in comfy_extras files, comfy_api_nodes glob-matched files, and external custom_nodes via load_custom_node().

Model/MLOps core lives under comfy/: model_detection.py fingerprints checkpoints from state-dict keys, model_management.py owns device/VRAM/pinning policy, model_patcher.py owns the ModelPatcher weight-patching abstraction, samplers.py/sample.py own the sampling loop, and ldm/ holds model implementations.

Persistent state: a SQLite database (default user/comfyui.db, override via --database-url) is created by app/database/db.py init_db() using SQLAlchemy + Alembic migrations in alembic_db/, guarded by a filelock <db>.lock against concurrent ComfyUI processes.

The web frontend is not in this repo: it ships as the pinned pip package comfyui-frontend-package==1.53.6 and FrontendManager.init_frontend() can download a release zip from api.github.com when --front-end-version requests a specific version; --front-end-root overrides with a local path.

CLI configuration is a module-level argparse parser in comfy/cli_args.py (~70 flags: --listen/--port, --cuda-device, VRAM modes, cache modes, dtype forcing, --disable-all-custom-nodes, --enable-manager, --database-url, --enable-assets) whose parsed `args` singleton is imported by nearly every module.

Directory layout is configured at import time in folder_paths.py: folder_names_and_paths maps logical model categories (checkpoints, loras, vae, diffusion_models, controlnet, upscale_models, ~20 total) to search dirs, plus output/temp/input/user dirs all relocatable via --base-directory or per-dir flags.

Runtime concurrency model: one asyncio event loop runs the HTTP server and a publish_loop() that drains a message queue fed thread-safely by send_sync() from the worker thread; WebSocket clients live in self.sockets keyed by clientId.

Optional sub-apps and managers attach in add_routes(): UserManager (/users, /userdata), ModelFileManager (/experiment/models), CustomNodeManager (/workflow_templates, /i18n), SubgraphManager, NodeReplaceManager, and an /internal sub-application from api_server InternalRoutes.

Build/run/test surface: pip install -r requirements.txt then `python main.py`; unit tests via `pytest tests-unit` (pytest.ini sets testpaths to tests and tests-unit); lint via ruff config in pyproject.toml and .github/workflows/ruff.yml.

feature_catalog.summary: The user-facing surface is an HTTP+WebSocket API driving a node-graph execution engine, plus a large built-in node library. HTTP covers prompt submission, queue/history management, job status, image upload/view, model listing, object_info schema introspection, user data storage, and workflow templates. The node catalog spans core SD nodes in nodes.py, ~130 comfy_extras modules (audio, video, 3D, model merging, advanced samplers), and comfy_api_nodes that call paid third-party APIs. The optional ComfyUI Manager integration and the assets system (blake3-hashed media catalog in SQLite) are feature-flagged subsystems.

claims.claim: POST /prompt accepts a workflow graph {node_id: {class_type, inputs}} plus optional client_id/extra_data/prompt_id/partial_execution_targets, runs validate_prompt, and heapq-pushes (number, prompt_id, prompt, extra_data, outputs_to_execute, sensitive) onto PromptQueue returning {prompt_id, number, node_errors}.

Queue and history endpoints: GET /queue returns running+pending with sensitive fields stripped by _remove_sensitive_from_queue; POST /queue supports clear/delete; GET /history and /history/{prompt_id} read the in-memory history dict; POST /history clears or deletes entries.

A jobs API exposes GET /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs/{job_id}, POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/cancel and POST /api/jobs/cancel backed by comfy_execution/jobs.py with JobStatus pending/in_progress/completed/failed/cancelled.

POST /interrupt either targets a specific running prompt_id or globally interrupts via nodes.interrupt_processing -> comfy.model_management.interrupt_current_processing; POST /free sets unload_models/free_memory flags consumed by the worker loop.

File endpoints: POST /upload/image and /upload/mask write into input/temp/output dirs with subfolder confinement checks and duplicate detection via hashing; GET /view serves files (including blake3: hash resolution to asset paths) and GET /view_metadata/{folder} exposes safetensors metadata.

Introspection endpoints: GET /object_info and /object_info/{node_class} serialize each node class's INPUT_TYPES/RETURN_TYPES/CATEGORY for the frontend; GET /models and /models/{folder} list folder_paths categories; GET /embeddings lists embedding names; GET /system_stats and /features report device and capability info.

The /ws WebSocket negotiates per-client feature_flags as the first message, then streams JSON events (status, executing, executed, progress, execution_start/cached/success/error) and binary frames for preview images (PREVIEW_IMAGE, UNENCODED_PREVIEW_IMAGE, PREVIEW_IMAGE_WITH_METADATA from protocol.BinaryEventTypes).

Core node set in nodes.py covers the SD1.x/SDXL workflow: CheckpointLoaderSimple, CLIPTextEncode, KSampler/KSamplerAdvanced, VAEEncode/VAEDecode(+Tiled), LoraLoader, ControlNetLoader/Apply, EmptyLatentImage, SaveImage/PreviewImage, LoadImage, and conditioning/latent/image transform nodes.

comfy_extras/ contributes ~130 node modules loaded by init_builtin_extra_nodes: upscale models, mask/compositing, model merging, SD3/Flux/Hunyuan/Wan/Qwen video+audio model support, 3D (load/save/mesh/gaussian splat), GLSL shaders, logic/loop/math utility nodes, and training nodes (nodes_train, nodes_dataset).

comfy_api_nodes/ contains API nodes that call remote paid services (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, Kling, Luma, ByteDance, ElevenLabs, Stability, etc.) authenticated through hidden AUTH_TOKEN_COMFY_ORG/API_KEY_COMFY_ORG extra_data keys; --disable-api-nodes blocks them and adds a restrictive CSP middleware.

User/file management features: UserManager adds /users CRUD and /userdata file endpoints (GET/POST/DELETE/move) gated by --multi-user; get_public_user_directory blocks '__'-prefixed system user dirs from HTTP access.

ModelFileManager adds experimental /experiment/models routes including a preview endpoint that extracts embedded preview images from model files; CustomNodeManager serves /workflow_templates and /i18n translation JSON built from loaded custom nodes.

The assets system (--enable-assets) registers uploads and generated outputs into a SQLite catalog with blake3 content hashes, runs background filesystem scans, and emits events through the server's send_sync sink.

Latent previews during sampling are produced by latent_preview.py with methods none/auto/latent2rgb/taesd chosen by --preview-method/--preview-size, streamed to the client as binary preview frames via the hijacked progress hook.
Internal (frontend-only, unstable) endpoints are mounted as the /internal sub-app: /internal/logs, /internal/logs/raw and log-subscription handled by TerminalService.

data_flow.summary: A prompt enters as JSON at POST /prompt, is validated into an executable output list, and becomes a heapq item on PromptQueue. The worker thread wraps it in DynamicPrompt (original + ephemeral + override layers) and builds an ExecutionList — a topological dissolve where nodes become ready when their link dependencies resolve. Each node call resolves inputs from cached upstream outputs, invokes the node's FUNCTION (mapped over input lists, async-aware), and stores outputs in signature-keyed caches; UI outputs and progress flow back over WebSocket via send_sync. Model weights flow through folder_paths resolvers into comfy.sd loaders that detect the architecture and wrap it in a ModelPatcher managed by model_management for VRAM offload. Results persist to the output dir (SaveImage) and the run record lands in the in-memory history dict (capped at 10000) plus the assets DB when enabled.

claims.claim: Input boundary: POST /prompt -> trigger_on_prompt(on_prompt_handlers) -> number assignment -> node_replace_manager.apply_replacements -> execution.validate_prompt -> PromptQueue.put((number, prompt_id, prompt, extra_data, outputs_to_execute, sensitive)).

validate_prompt collects OUTPUT_NODE classes (optionally filtered by partial_execution_targets), recursively validates inputs (type matching via validate_node_input, min/max, combo membership, custom VALIDATE_INPUTS/validate_inputs hooks), detects dependency cycles, and validates loop boundaries via validate_loops.

Execution loop: PromptExecutor.execute_async wraps everything in torch.inference_mode, builds DynamicPrompt + ExecutionList, seeds it with output node ids, then repeatedly calls stage_node_execution -> module-level execute() -> complete/unstage until the list empties.

Per-node execution order inside execute(): check output cache -> get_input_data resolves each input link through execution_list.get_cache (missing -> mark_missing and lazy evaluation via check_lazy_status returns PENDING) -> instantiate/cache the node object in caches.objects -> get_output_data -> _async_map_node_over_list -> node FUNCTION.

Intermediate results are cached by CacheSet: outputs cache uses CacheKeySetInputSignature (class_type + IS_CHANGED value + ancestor input signatures, folded via to_hashable) while objects cache uses CacheKeySetID (node_id, class_type); modes are CLASSIC/LRU/NONE/RAM_PRESSURE chosen by --cache-* flags.

Node functions can return plain tuples, dicts with 'result'/'ui'/'expand', or V3 NodeOutput objects; 'expand' produces an ephemeral subgraph injected into DynamicPrompt.ephemeral_prompt and re-scheduled, with the node's final outputs resolved later from pending_subgraph_results.

Streaming output: nodes emit UI data via 'ui' dicts -> register_executed_outputs enriches them into asset references -> send_sync('executed', ...) to the client; sampler progress goes through comfy.utils.ProgressBar global hook -> send_sync('progress') + binary preview frames.

Model loading path: folder_paths.get_full_path_or_raise resolves a filename inside a category's search dirs -> comfy.utils.load_torch_file reads safetensors/ckpt -> model_detection.model_config_from_unet fingerprints the state dict -> comfy.supported_models builds the model -> ModelPatcher wraps it -> load_models_gpu places it per VRAM policy.

Sampling path inside a node: KSampler.sample -> common_ksampler -> comfy.sample.prepare_noise (seeded) -> latent_preview.prepare_callback -> comfy.sample.sample -> comfy.samplers.KSampler.sample drives the denoise loop calling model.apply_model per sigma step.

History persistence: task_done() pops currently_running, strips the sensitive tuple element via process_item=remove_sensitive, and stores {prompt, outputs, status} in self.history keyed by prompt_id, evicting FIFO beyond MAXIMUM_HISTORY_SIZE=10000.

Auth-sensitive extra_data keys (auth_token_comfy_org, api_key_comfy_org) are popped into a separate `sensitive` dict at enqueue time, reattached only inside the worker, and injected into node inputs via hidden input plumbing (Hidden.auth_token_comfy_org / hidden AUTH_TOKEN_COMFY_ORG).

File output boundary: SaveImage writes PNGs (with embedded prompt/workflow metadata unless --disable-metadata) into folder_paths.get_output_directory() with counter-suffixed filenames; LoadImage reads from the input directory through annotated_filepath/get_annotated_filepath resolvers.

Asset enrichment: when enabled, AssetManager pauses its background scan during execution, registers uploaded/executed files into the DB catalog, and /view resolves blake3:<hash> filenames to asset paths via resolve_hash_to_path.

behavior_traces.summary: Traced flows: (1) startup from `python main.py` through arg parsing, env setup, prestartup scripts, node loading, DB init, route registration and server bind; (2) a prompt's journey from POST /prompt through validation, queueing, per-node execution, caching and WebSocket events; (3) model loading from a CheckpointLoaderSimple node through state-dict detection into a VRAM-managed ModelPatcher; (4) interrupt and memory-pressure handling; (5) image upload and /view retrieval with traversal guards.

claims.claim: Startup order: comfy.options.enable_args_parsing -> args parse -> setup_logger -> (optional) comfy_aimdo.control.init for DynamicVRAM -> apply_custom_paths (extra_model_paths.yaml, dir overrides) -> init_mime_types -> execute_prestartup_script over custom_nodes -> import execution/server/nodes -> start_comfyui: PromptServer(loop) -> init_extra_nodes -> set_cudnn_benchmark -> setup_database(init_db + asset_manager.startup) -> add_routes -> hijack_progress -> prompt_worker thread -> prompt_server.setup + run -> TCPSite bind on --listen/--port.

Prompt submission order: post_prompt -> request.json -> trigger_on_prompt -> client prompt_id validation via validate_job_id (canonical UUID) -> node_replace_manager.apply_replacements -> validate_prompt -> sensitive key extraction -> prompt_queue.put -> queue_updated() broadcasts status -> worker q.get pops the item.

Worker execution order: prompt_worker gets item -> asset_manager.pause_background_scan -> PromptExecutor.execute -> execute_async: set_preview_method -> interrupt_processing(False) -> execution_start msg -> torch.inference_mode -> DynamicPrompt + reset_progress_state -> caches.set_prompt/clean_unused -> execution_cached msg -> loop stage_node_execution/execute -> execution_success or handle_execution_error -> task_done stores history -> send 'executing' node=None.

Single node step order inside execute(): dynprompt id mapping (real/display/parent) -> caches.outputs.get short-circuit -> get_input_data (links via execution_list.get_cache, hidden PROMPT/DYNPROMPT/EXTRA_PNGINFO/UNIQUE_ID injection) -> send 'executing' -> lazy check via check_lazy_status -> get_output_data -> _async_map_node_over_list (slices list inputs, asyncio.create_task for coroutine functions, ExecutionBlocker propagation) -> merge_result_data -> caches.outputs.set + execution_list.cache_update -> 'executed' event.

Interrupt trace: POST /interrupt -> nodes.interrupt_processing -> comfy.model_management.interrupt_current_processing(True) -> flag checked by throw_exception_if_processing_interrupted inside the progress hook and before_node_execution -> InterruptProcessingException caught in execute() -> handle_execution_error sends 'execution_interrupted'.

Checkpoint load trace: CheckpointLoaderSimple node -> comfy.sd.load_checkpoint_guess_config -> utils.load_torch_file -> model_detection.unet_prefix_from_state_dict + model_config_from_unet (state-dict key/shape fingerprinting) -> model_config classes from comfy.supported_models -> CLIP/VAE patchers built -> ModelPatcher returned as MODEL output -> later load_models_gpu/free_memory decide device placement and weight offloading.

Image upload trace: POST /upload/image -> request.post() -> image_upload -> get_dir_by_type(input/temp/output) -> normpath join + commonpath containment check -> hash-compare dedup loop renaming 'name (i).ext' -> write file -> asset_manager.register_upload -> JSON {name, subfolder, type, asset?}.

WebSocket lifecycle: GET /ws -> ws.prepare -> sid from clientId query or uuid4 -> sockets[sid]=ws -> send 'status' with queue info -> first TEXT message may carry feature_flags (stored in sockets_metadata, server flags replied) -> all server->client traffic funnels through send_sync -> messages queue -> publish_loop -> send_json/send_bytes.

OOM/error path: exception inside execute() -> formatted inputs captured -> comfy.model_management.is_oom check triggers unload_all_models and debug_memory_summary logging -> error_details {node_id, exception_message, exception_type, traceback, current_inputs} -> handle_execution_error -> 'execution_error' WebSocket message -> worker records status 'error' in history.

RAM-pressure caching behavior: with default RAM_PRESSURE cache, execute_async wires ram_release callback into memory_management.set_ram_cache_release_state; after each node it releases toward inactive headroom, computes shortfall vs virtual_memory_available, frees large intermediates then pins if needed.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is pytest-based and split into two trees: tests-unit (fast unit tests, run in CI on Linux/Windows/macOS with CPU torch) and tests (integration: execution tests that spawn a real server subprocess and drive it over WebSocket, and inference tests that run full workflows and compare generated images against a baseline directory). Markers 'inference' and 'execution' allow deselection. Coverage of the node library itself is thin — most tests target the execution engine, validation, caching, and server endpoints rather than model math.

claims.claim: pytest.ini sets testpaths to both tests and tests-unit, registers 'inference' and 'execution' markers, and adds -s (no output capture); pythonpath=. makes the repo root importable.

tests/execution/test_execution.py spins up the real server via subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, 'main.py', ...]), waits, connects a ComfyClient over websocket-client, submits prompt graphs built with GraphBuilder, and asserts on WS events and output images.

tests/execution also covers async nodes, jobs API, preview method override, progress isolation, and the public API (test_public_api.py), with a testing_nodes helper package of custom nodes for the tests.

tests/inference/test_inference.py runs real diffusion workflows (ComfyGraph wrapper, KSampler imported from comfy.samplers) writing images to --output_dir; tests/compare performs quality regression by comparing directories, and conftest.py deliberately runs test_quality last.

tests-unit covers the execution engine (test_execution_list, validate_node_input, loop validation, nested loops, cache providers, reentry), server/user endpoints (prompt_server_test, system_user_endpoint_test), folder_paths, security (security_test dir), assets, and comfy internals — all CPU-only.

CI: .github/workflows/test-unit.yml runs `pytest tests-unit` on ubuntu-latest/windows-2022/macos-latest with Python 3.12 and CPU-only torch; it is marked continue-on-error, so unit failures do not block merges.

Additional workflows: test-execution.yml and test-ci.yml run the execution/integration suites, test-launch.yml smoke-tests server launch (--quick-test-for-ci exits after startup), and ruff.yml lints with the rule set pinned in pyproject.toml.

Test deps are separate: tests-unit/requirements.txt plus websocket-client/opencv/scikit-image for integration tests per tests/README.md; inference tests require downloaded models, so they are not runnable in plain CI.

No coverage tooling, no mocked-HTTP layer for aiohttp routes, and no tests under comfy/ for individual model implementations — model correctness is only exercised indirectly through the heavyweight inference suite.
A --quick-test-for-ci flag in main.py exits right after the worker thread starts, which is what test-launch.yml uses to verify the server boots cleanly.

risk_map.summary: Biggest risks: there is no authentication on the HTTP API, custom nodes are arbitrary code executed at startup, and model file formats include pickle-capable extensions. The codebase has accumulated scattered path-traversal and XSS mitigations that must be replicated at every new file endpoint. The execution engine is a single shared mutable state machine (server.client_id, last_node_id, module-level registries) so concurrent or reentrant use is fragile. Memory management and the aimdo/DynamicVRAM integration contain version-dependent protocol fallbacks that are easy to break.

claims.claim: No authentication exists on any route: default bind is 127.0.0.1, but --listen with no value exposes 0.0.0.0,:: — an unauthenticated API that can queue prompts, read/write userdata files, upload images, and hit /internal/logs.

Custom nodes are arbitrary Python: execute_prestartup_script exec_modules every custom_nodes/*/prestartup_script.py before the server starts, and load_custom_node exec_modules each module — remote-code-execution by design; mitigations are only --disable-all-custom-nodes/--whitelist-custom-nodes and optional comfyui_manager policy.
supported_pt_extensions includes .ckpt/.pt/.bin/.pkl — formats that can embed pickle payloads; loading relies on comfy.utils.load_torch_file's safe handling, so changes there are security-critical.

Path traversal defenses are reimplemented per endpoint: /view checks '..' and leading '/', subfolder joins use os.path.commonpath containment, and folder_paths.is_within_directory/get_annotated_filepath add realpath-based containment — any new file-serving endpoint must repeat this correctly.

Stored-XSS mitigation is centralized in folder_paths.DANGEROUS_CONTENT_TYPES/is_dangerous_content_type with a Sec-Fetch-Dest:image carve-out for SVG; endpoints serving user content must route dangerous types to octet-stream or they reintroduce XSS.

origin_only_middleware is an admitted partial fix for DNS-rebinding/cross-site POSTs to a loopback server ('the proper fix would be to add a cookie'): it 403s Sec-Fetch-Site:cross-site and Host/Origin hostname mismatches only when Host resolves to loopback.

Shared mutable globals: server.client_id and last_node_id are single-slot fields on PromptServer set from extra_data of whichever prompt is running, and NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS is a module-level dict mutated by every extension — one concurrently executing prompt or a misbehaving custom node can corrupt routing/display state.
comfy_aimdo protocol drift is handled by chained TypeError fallbacks (0.4.9/0.4.10 signatures) in main.py; silent wrong-version behavior is a real hazard since the fallbacks catch TypeError broadly.

The queue item is a positional tuple where index 5 is `sensitive` extra data; _remove_sensitive_from_queue and the remove_sensitive lambda both rely on tuple position, so reordering the tuple silently leaks auth tokens into queue/history responses.

hook_breaker_ac10a0.py is a manual save/restore shim that protects comfy.model_management.cast_to from being hooked by custom nodes — evidence that custom-node monkeypatching has caused production incidents and protection is opt-in per function.

DB init kills the process on lock contention only when --enable-assets is set; otherwise it logs and continues with a degraded assets layer — divergence between code paths makes failures mode-dependent.
Alembic migration 0007_record_content_split is explicitly destructive: upgrading through it discards the prior asset catalog (tags, metadata, previews, renames) keeping only a .bkp file.

API nodes make outbound calls to dozens of paid third-party services using the user's comfy-org token; --disable-api-nodes exists as the kill switch and also adds a strict CSP header, implying these nodes are treated as the network-risk boundary.

extension_points.summary: ComfyUI's primary extension mechanism is the custom_nodes directory scanned at startup: V1 extensions export NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS/NODE_DISPLAY_NAME_MAPPINGS dicts (and optional WEB_DIRECTORY for frontend JS), while V3 extensions expose a comfy_entrypoint() returning a ComfyExtension whose get_node_list() yields ComfyNode classes with declarative Schemas. Secondary hooks: prestartup_script.py per package, server.on_prompt_handlers for prompt mutation, custom aiohttp routes via PromptServer.instance.routes, extra model paths via yaml config, progress handlers, cache providers, and node replacement rules.

claims.claim: V1 node contract: a module in custom_nodes/ exporting NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS {name: class} where each class defines INPUT_TYPES (required/optional/hidden), RETURN_TYPES, FUNCTION (method name), CATEGORY; OUTPUT_NODE=True makes it an execution target; registered into the global registry by load_custom_node.

V3 node contract: modules export comfy_entrypoint() (sync or async) returning a ComfyExtension; get_node_list() returns io.ComfyNode subclasses whose GET_SCHEMA() provides node_id, inputs/outputs as typed Input/Output objects, hidden flags, and behavior flags (is_output_node, not_idempotent, enable_expand, accept_all_inputs, loop_boundary).

Frontend extension point: WEB_DIRECTORY module attr or pyproject.toml [tool.comfy] web dir registers a static JS dir served at /extensions/<name>; /extensions endpoint enumerates all JS for the frontend to import.
Per-package prestartup hook: any custom_nodes/<pkg>/prestartup_script.py is exec'd before node loading, letting packages patch the environment early (used e.g. for dependency installs).
Prompt mutation hook: PromptServer.add_on_prompt_handler registers callables run by trigger_on_prompt on every POST /prompt body before validation (exceptions are logged and skipped).
HTTP route extension: custom nodes can append to PromptServer.instance.routes (the same RouteTableDef), and every added route is automatically mirrored under /api by add_routes.

Model path extension: extra_model_paths.yaml (example in repo root) and --extra-model-paths-config call utils.extra_config.load_extra_path_config which feeds folder_paths.add_model_folder_path to add search dirs per category.

Execution hooks for nodes: IS_CHANGED/fingerprint_inputs controls cache reuse; check_lazy_status marks required inputs for lazy evaluation; VALIDATE_INPUTS/validate_inputs custom-validates; ExecutionBlocker short-circuits branches; GraphBuilder lets a node emit an 'expand' subgraph.

Cache providers: comfy_execution/cache_provider.py exposes _get_cache_providers()/_has_cache_providers and PromptExecutor calls provider.on_prompt_start/on_prompt_end around each run — an external cache persistence seam.
Progress reporting is extensible via add_progress_handler in comfy_execution/progress.py; WebUIProgressHandler is the built-in implementation forwarding to the websocket client.

Feature flags: comfy_api/feature_flags.py maintains CLI_FEATURE_FLAG_REGISTRY (--list-feature-flag dumps it) and per-connection negotiation lets clients declare capabilities like supports_preview_metadata that change server behavior.

Comfy API versioning seam: comfy_api/version_list.supported_versions are registered through register_versions(ComfyAPIWithVersion) in init_public_apis, letting custom nodes target a stable versioned API surface (v0_0_1, v0_0_2, latest).
NodeReplaceManager rewrites submitted prompt graphs (apply_replacements is invoked in post_prompt before validation) — a server-side node-substitution extension point.
comfyui_manager is an optional pip-installed extension enabled by --enable-manager that adds its own middleware, prestartup, and node-load policy hooks (should_be_disabled).

agent_handoff.summary: AGENTS.md is unusually prescriptive and is the first file to read: it demands minimal diffs, no new dependencies, no outbound network calls in core, strict layer boundaries (execution.py must not learn API/persistence concepts), no torch.no_grad wrappers (inference_mode already wraps execution), and reuse of comfy.ops/quant_ops/Comfy Kitchen optimized ops for model code. Read main.py -> server.py -> execution.py -> nodes.py -> folder_paths.py -> comfy/cli_args.py to understand any user-facing change. Tests: pytest tests-unit for fast checks; tests/execution needs a spawned server; tests/inference needs real models. Watch the traps: import-time side effects everywhere, tuple-indexed queue items, three different node ids (real/display/ephemeral), and signature-based caching that silently reuses outputs.

claims.claim: AGENTS.md mandates: smallest possible diff, no new dependencies, no internet requests from core ComfyUI (no telemetry/upload/update-check code paths), and aggressive deletion of dead compat code.

AGENTS.md architecture rule: keep layer boundaries — execution.py consumes the prompt graph and must not know workflow/frontend/persistence ids; fix leaks with caller-side mapping or narrow interfaces rather than passing context objects through.

AGENTS.md model rules: never add torch.no_grad/inference_mode wrappers (execution is already inside torch.inference_mode), never add freeze/trainability toggles, prefer existing optimized ops in comfy.ops/comfy.quant_ops/Comfy Kitchen, and DiT models must tolerate non-patch-multiple latents via pad_to_patch_size.

Import order is load-bearing: torch must not be imported before main.py's late import block (it warns if 'torch' is in sys.modules), which is why ExecutionBlocker lives in comfy_execution/graph_utils.py rather than graph.py — keep heavy imports out of modules parsed early.

The args singleton from comfy.cli_args is parsed at import time and read by folder_paths at import time to fix base_path/models_dir — tests and embedding code must control argv or env carefully; comfy.options.enable_args_parsing() is the gate.

Queue tuple layout is positional and load-bearing: (number, prompt_id, prompt, extra_data, outputs_to_execute, sensitive); index 5 is stripped before exposure — preserve arity when modifying put/get/task_done or the remove_sensitive lambdas.

Three node-id namespaces coexist: ephemeral ids (created by expand), display ids (UI mapping), and real ids (original prompt); always use dynprompt.get_real_node_id/get_display_node_id rather than raw ids in execution code.

Caching can silently skip your code path: outputs are keyed by input signature including IS_CHANGED/fingerprint_inputs — when debugging a node that 'doesn't run', check CacheKeySetInputSignature and the node flags NOT_IDEMPOTENT / UNIQUE_ID hidden input first.

Safe edit boundaries: add a node in nodes.py or a comfy_extras/nodes_*.py file (register in NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS), add routes in the owning app/* manager, add model support via comfy/model_detection.py signature + comfy/supported_models entry — do not create parallel registries.

Run `pytest tests-unit` after changes; unit CI is continue-on-error so green CI does not prove correctness — for executor changes also run tests/execution which needs websocket-client and spawns main.py as a subprocess.

When touching file-serving endpoints, reuse folder_paths.is_within_directory/get_annotated_filepath and is_dangerous_content_type rather than hand-rolling checks — traversal/XSS guards are the most-reviewed security surface.
Style: ruff lint (E, W, F, T print-usage, S102/S307, N805) with E501/E722/E731/E402 ignored; comments sparse; match local style — long lines and module-level state are normal here.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in ComfyUI (python main.py), a single-process node-graph inference engine for diffusion/generative models. Architecture: main.py parses the module-level argparse singleton in comfy/cli_args.py, sets device env vars, execs custom-node prestartup_script.py files, loads all node registries via nodes.init_extra_nodes (core nodes.py + ~130 comfy_extras files + comfy_api_nodes + custom_nodes/), initializes an Alembic-managed SQLite DB (user/comfyui.db, filelock-guarded), then starts server.PromptServer (aiohttp) and a daemon prompt_worker thread.

Request flow: POST /prompt JSON -> validate_prompt (type/min-max/combo/cycle/loop checks) -> heapq PromptQueue -> worker -> execution.PromptExecutor.execute_async under torch.inference_mode -> DynamicPrompt + ExecutionList topological dissolve -> per-node execute(): cache lookup -> get_input_data (links, hidden inputs) -> node FUNCTION via _async_map_node_over_list -> CacheEntry stored in signature-keyed caches -> 'executed'/'progress' WS events via send_sync -> publish_loop -> history dict (cap 10000).

Key invariants: queue items are positional tuples with sensitive extra_data at index 5 (auth_token_comfy_org, api_key_comfy_org) stripped before any exposure; three node id namespaces (real/display/ephemeral) must go through DynamicPrompt helpers; node output caching is keyed by class_type + IS_CHANGED + ancestor input signatures so identical inputs reuse results — flag nondeterminism with NOT_IDEMPOTENT or UNIQUE_ID hidden input.

Extension points: V1 nodes export NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS + INPUT_TYPES/RETURN_TYPES/FUNCTION; V3 nodes export comfy_entrypoint() -> ComfyExtension -> ComfyNode classes with GET_SCHEMA; WEB_DIRECTORY registers frontend JS at /extensions/<name>; on_prompt_handlers mutate prompt JSON; extra_model_paths.yaml adds model search dirs via folder_paths.add_model_folder_path.

Rules (from AGENTS.md): minimal diffs, no new deps, no outbound network code in core, no torch.no_grad/inference_mode wrappers, no einops in model code, preserve node names/APIs/workflow compat, reuse comfy.ops/quant_ops/Comfy Kitchen ops, keep execution.py free of API/persistence concepts. Torch must not be imported before main.py's late import block. Security surface: folder_paths.is_within_directory + annotated_filepath + DANGEROUS_CONTENT_TYPES are the traversal/XSS toolkit — reuse them at every file endpoint; there is no auth, default bind is 127.0.0.1.

Test: `pytest tests-unit` (CPU-only, CI matrix is continue-on-error); tests/execution spawns the real server over WebSocket; tests/inference needs real models and does image regression against a baseline dir. Lint: ruff (config in pyproject.toml).
